text_fidelity_a:
Firmstrong Bruiser Man Single Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle This bike has turned out to be a very good purchase for me.

I live on my boat in Los Angles and am able to attend to 90% of my brick and mortar shopping without using my car since this bike is beefy and has no problem handling a couple of saddle bag type baskets as well as a basket on the handlebars. A 36 pack of canned beer rides securely on the rear rack held in place with bungee cords

I bought the three speed model and am glad I did. Even though the area around us is pretty flat there are a few sloped ramps, on our great local bike paths, that make me appreciate the ability to shift down. Down wind on a level surface, or down hill, the high gear is useful. Some days the breeze off the ocean is strong enough to cause me to shift down when headed up wind. The three speed has no derailleur so the bike has a chain guard.

This bike is very easy to ride and takes a lot of the back and hand stress out of riding my bike. Im 72 and outgrew dropped handlebars about half a century ago.

It took me a few days to get used to coaster brakes again, after decades of cool bikes with hand brakes. But now Im cool with the coaster brake and really like the lack of clutter on the handle bars.

I added a bell, lights and a holder for my smart phone. I also added a really nice rear view mirror which is a great safety feature. I got a nice beefy lock on Amazon and really like the fact that I can drop it in my basket instead of going to the trouble of installing it on the mount on the bike every time I take off.

Since I live in southern California fenders seemed pointless so I skipped that accessory.

The bike is easy to ride with its big tires but is not fast. If you want a fast bike a beach cruiser is probably not what you should buy.

Unless I have some compelling reason to get in my car I do all my local travel on my bike. Its easier, faster many times, and there are no parking hassles or cost. I rode it 25 miles round trip to a doctor appointment a week ago. It was along the beach where there is a nice bike path and lots of scenery. It was not an exhausting experience but then I was not in a big hurry.

As I ride to the gym every morning Im passed by cyclists on high tech bikes who are bent into incredibly uncomfortable looking positions over their dropped handle bars. As they zoom past I reflect on the fact that I definitely bought the right bike for me and also that some people should not be wearing lycra cycling outfits.

The only negative about this purchase was that the packaging on the bike was not adequate to protect it in shipment. The three speed shifter on the rear axel had broken through the cardboard box and got scratched up in shipment. The damage did not look like it was more than cosmetic and I did not want o hassle with repacking the bike to return it so I went ahead and accepted as it was.
text_fidelity_b: Firmstrong Bruiser Man Single Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle

text_fidelity_a:
LifeSpan Fitness Folding Treadmill Easy to assemble, rock solid, delivery experience was good (they delivery guys went above and beyond and brought it all the way to the room where I needed it).

I think the shocks other reviewers are talking about are just normal static shocks from dry air and belt friction. It's not a dangerous kind of thing and I would expect any treadmill to have this problem in winter.

I've been using it for running and walking. I built a desk shelf for it and use it as a treadmill desk while working and as a running trainer at other times. I'm 240 pounds and it doesn't have any problem at all with my weight. I like the programmable workout programs that let you set up arbitrary incline and speed changes over the course of a workout.

The handheld heart monitors seem to be pretty inaccurate for me (dangerously underestimating my heart rate even when I'm working out really hard). I got the chest band heart monitor and it works great and seems to be much more accurate. You need to order the chest band from lifespan, I don't know if it works with other ones.

EDIT - I am deducting 1 star from this treadmill because for some dumb reason after 99 minutes and 59 seconds of walking it shuts down. It beeps and shuts down instantly, no slow down, which is jarring and unsafe. So this makes it not ideal as a treadmill desk (your workout isn't likely to be longer than 99 minutes, but your work day certain is!). I can't find any way in the settings to disable this flaw. I know there's only digits for 99 minutes on the display but there's no reason not to just let the belt keep running even after the display maxes out - could leave it stuck at 99:59 or could wrap around to 0 or could switch to hours:minutes at that point but instead it does the unsafe thing of immediately stopping.

EDIT2 - I am deducting another star because their customer service's response to my complaint about the 99 minutes issue was that I should buy another different treadmill from them! It seems like this would be so easy to address via a firmware update.
text_fidelity_b: LifeSpan Fitness Folding Treadmill

Innova Inversion Table with Adjustable Headrest, Reversible Ankle Holders, and 300 lb Weight Capacity I don't have any particular back problems I was trying to address, but this has felt good to use. I have been doing the inversion at 45 degrees for a minute or two at a time, two or three times a day. I tried 60 degrees, but 45 is best for me. The table is sturdy overall, thought the leg and foot mechanism is a little shaky (I would not trust it if I were close to the 300 pound limit). It was easy to assemble - you just need to take your time and follow each step of the instructions carefully. There is one step that requires two people.
I am 6 feet tall and about 180 pounds. If I set the adjustable height at 6'2", I get perfect balance.
What I dislike is the head rest. It doesn't matter which setting is used to adjust it, the problem is just that it has a headrest that is thicker then the body. If the goal is to invert and allow pressure to come off the the neck and back, why do I want something forcing my neck to jut forward instead of being freely aligned with my back. If you are thinking of buying this to help with your neck, I would recommend a table that is flat - the neck and back supported at the same level (when horizontal, of course). I have enjoyed the inversion table, and have no problems with it's overall quality. I wish I had purchased a different one, though, due to the headrest.
text_fidelity_b: Innova Inversion Table with Adjustable Headrest, Reversible Ankle Holders, and 300 lb Weight Capacity

Although I’ve only been pool swimming a few years, I’ve gone scuba diving around the world and worked in the visual arts professionally many years I’m highly sensitized and particular visually.

After reading many swim goggle reviews on amazon, fumbling my way through to find a great pair, thankfully I came across a guy who is an avid swimmer and asserted he never even considers lenses that aren’t flat. It got me thinking… What’s that about?

It’s those funky lenses you see pro swimmers were - for a reason! Everything becomes crystal clear when you put a flat lens goggles on. These are not sunglasses or eyeglasses. Swim goggles are made from very different material that annoy does not uphold clarity when bent. No matter who makes them. (Hence the pros will only wear them..now you’re getting it ;)

I simply couldn’t believe how magically everything became beautifully clear and visible when I put the flat lens goggles on. It’s like wiping grease from a window that becomes a big picture window! All of a sudden you see all the beauty of the sky above, your surroundings, and dancing sunlight under the waterline while you swim!!

(I’m my pic they’re the ones on top)

Whichever brand you buy - BUY FLAT LENS SWIM GOGGLES!!

text_fidelity_a: SoundAsleep Camping Series Air Mattress with Eco-Friendly PVC - Included Rechargeable Air Pump - Queen Size I'm always wary of buying air mattresses since I've never had one last more than a couple seasons before constantly deflating during the night. I hope this one is different, and so far after 4 nights it's performed beautifully. The mattress is very comfortable and I noticed that part of the reason for this is that the air chambers go from side to side instead of lengthwise like some other models. This seems to different zones for support and I'll look for this in any future air mattress purchases. I experienced very little initial stretching which the instructions say is common for the first few nights. I slept on it for 3 nights and only added a tiny bit of air the last night just to see how firm it would get. A nice touch is that the sides are slightly higher than the middle, which is very subtle but I'm sure keeps you from rolling off during the night. It comes with a good quality storage bag which sould help protect it when stored. The rechargable pump works well for inflating and deflating and comes with an AC adapter, car charger, and a couple different nozzles. Actually, the charger is the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars - for two reasons. First, it has NiCd batteries which are pretty old school in terms of rechargeables and won't last very long, at which point it becomes a brick. Ominously, perhaps they are only meant to last as long as the mattress? Second, the charger and accessories don't come with any kind of stuff sack or even a pocket in the mattress bag. I nice little cheapo storage sack for the charger and accessories is really needed. Other than that, so far so good. Very comfortable mattress.
text_fidelity_b: SoundAsleep Camping Series Air Mattress with Eco-Friendly PVC - Included Rechargeable Air Pump - Queen Size

text_fidelity_a:
Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch Here I am again, this time I'm looking for the best pouch possible for a very specific carry option. I've wanted something to carry one of my home made mini EDC kits, plus a few other items. I've found some really nice models, but they were usually too big or too small. Some were a great size for my needs, but were cost prohibitive.

Alas, I found a Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch on Amazon for about $14. I had narrowed it down to this item over a Condor Gadget MOLLE Pouch. The prices were nearly identical, so I went over both items with a discerning eye. The Monstrum was about a half-inch smaller, so it was a close call.

I believe some Monstrum products mimic their higher priced competition, yet still make a great value. There may be subtle differences here and there, but there were no major must-haves. I rarely go for the high end products when I find one that is similar for a lower price and good reviews. A quick note on reviews? Take them ALL with a grain of salt.

The Monstrum pouch appears to be very well made. The stitching appears sturdy and I only found one loose thread, which I burned down in about 3 seconds. It was a small detail, but it lent itself to the overall quality. The zippers, zipper pulls, and Velcro patches are also solid.

Features on the pouch were way more than I expected and what I saw online. As I looked it over, right after opening the Amazon box, I knew I had hit a homerun. From the front, there is a hard pouch cover with a zippered pocket. On the underside of that cover is a heavy duty patch of Velcro that connects to the front, expandable, pocket. On either side of that pocket are elastic loops that can be adjusted to hold the pocket tightly closed. In this front area, you have it subdivided into different sections. Behind this front area, you have the main pocket. It has 3 subdivisions and they held everything I wanted with a tiny bit of room left. This main pocket has two zippers w/pulls. On the back of the pouch, there are two MOLLE snap straps, which are useful to wear on a belt, if you know how to weave them correctly.

One of the main things that I liked was the expandable front pocket. It really protrudes as you add more stuff, so those adjustable elastic straps help it stay secure. It more than serves its purpose.

Pros:
Cost @ $14
Strong & sturdy
Perfect size for a mini-EDC kit and other small items
Multiple carry options

Cons:
It looks pregnant with all the stuff I put in there, so that's a bit odd.
(As was that statement).

Final verdict? Take a close look for yourself on the Monstrum or Amazon websites and see for yourself. If you have a couple of handfuls of small-ish gear you want to keep in its own pouch, this may work out perfect for you too.
text_fidelity_b: Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch

text_fidelity_a:
YAKIMA, ForkLift Fork Mount Bike Carrier for Roof Racks, 1 Bike Capacity I bought one of these racks in June 2017 from REI, and have used it many times over the year. The rack is a good solution for my Mazda 5 roof bars, though it's somewhat challenging to get my fairly heavy Electra Townie on and off the car (I'm not a strong person).

I bought a second rack recently (December 2017). The new rack has a different "skewer" design than the old one. The old skewer had a "cap" on one end, and the locking/folding head screws on and off. The new skewer has the locking/folding head fixed to the bolt, and the cap on the opposite side screws on and off. My problem with the new design is that it's simply not as secure as the old one. With a lock core fitted and locked, the old locking head simply cannot be removed when a bike is clamped in (well, it could be by somebody with a hacksaw or something, but it's at least conceptually a sound system). Because the new skewer has a screw-off cap opposite the locking end, the lock is irrelevant: the screw can simply be removed and the bike is free.

The attached photo shows the old skewer ("A" and "B" for the locking head and the fixed end cap), and the new skewer ("C" for the locking head and "D" is the screw-off endcap).

Update: I heard back from Yakima support. Apparently there's a mechanism in the new endcap on the skewer that does pretty much what the spring-loaded sleeve on the old locking mechanism did. When the cap is tight against the fork, it actually cannot be removed at all easily. So two stars back :)
text_fidelity_b: YAKIMA, ForkLift Fork Mount Bike Carrier for Roof Racks, 1 Bike Capacity

Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent Prior to getting this tent we borrowed a tent for a camping trip, and while we thought it set up quick and seemed nice, we were greeted by a deluge pouring through the seams on the roof. My wife was about ready to swear off camping, but we pushed on. We weren't going to let that happen again, so when I saw this tent, I pounced.

It comes in a rather large box, and the bag within is big for a four person tent, but not too large. The real bonus was the expanding bottom of the bag, which makes it nice and neat for before the sale but expands to be a more realistic container after the first trip, where things don't tend to fit in their original bags.

That trip was eye opening. Not only is the sixty second assembly more or less legit (it kinda doubles when you include taking it out of the bag), it's an ample tent. I'm 6'7" and while I couldn't stand in in the tent, it's broad tall roof is such a blessing. Likewise the sides go up at a steep angle making all but the outer inches rather tall too. It's nice and airy and makes a very generous two person tent, though you could turn it into a flop house and squeeze 4 in. I'd say 4 is doable, and 2 is luxurious, which is more than I'd say for any 4 person tents. Well done!

No leaks, quick setup, quick break down, and stylish looks are a big pluses.

Minuses are few and minor--mostly size of tent for storage (as the description notes, this isn't for backpacking). It's not the most compact, but really it's a slight difference and the quick setup is a great trade off and makes you want to actually use the tent!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent

text_fidelity_a:
Thule DoubleTrack Pro XT 2 Hitch Bike Rack I have no one to blame but myself for trusting this rack would be suitable.
As others have noted, the single post with two locking hook design makes it very very difficult to mount two same frame height bikes simultaneously. But what's worse is that there's no easy way to load the bikes on the rack! If the locking post is upright, then the hook gets in the way of the bike. If the post is lying flat, then once you've put your bikes on there is no way to raise the post without removing the hooks first. Also, you can't keep the bike standing upright while moving the post, because the tire obstructs the locking hook, so you need to be prepared to have the bike lean on your car trunk. What a design disaster.
Make sure to try the rack before you buy. None of the youtube videos will point out these issues. And those guys showing how they easily get their ebikes on the rack? Good luck with that. You'll need to be in pretty good shape to do that heavy lifting.

I've gotten into rebuilding old 80's BMX bicycles in the last year (6 of them total) and this tool has been great for installing headsets, tightening bottom brackets, and even holding detanglers in place. While not available currently on Amazon, I think I paid like $6 for it. Expecting very little, but for the 10-12 times I've used it, was a Godsend.

I think I even caught myself using it to loosen a axle nut on my truck, when I didn't have a wrench large enough. Couple taps with a rubber mallet and it worked wonderfully.

Headsets and bottom brackets should be finger tight, then a 1/4 to 1/2 turn with a wrench most of the time. A light touch. If you're torquing them down, you'll likely crush the bearings. Or at least restrict their movement.

This wrench - for the price - works great for my needs. Would definitely buy again.

Klean Kanteen Single Wall Stainless Steel Food Canister Container with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Lid I love this canister! It is heavy, sturdy and incredibly durable. This is my fourth purchase from the Klean Kanteen company and I've been incredibly pleased with everything I have purchased. This canister is no exception!

I got tired of knocking over the orange box of baking soda in my pantry and began looking for a stainless storage jar. Most of the stainless pantry jars had poor reviews and were so thin you could deform them with your bare hands. I wanted something that could withstand lots of bangs and bumps if I decided to throw the baking soda in the chuck box for a camp out. (Baking soda + water makes a great first aid paste for bites and stings.) When I stumbled across this one, I knew it would be ideal.

The 16 ounce canister easily held the full 16 ounce (1 pound) box of baking soda with room leftover to stash a small scoop. At 3.75 inches tall and 3.5 inches wide, it doesn't take up a ton of room on my pantry shelf but I no longer have to deal with gritty white baking soda spilling all over the tile floor of my pantry and lingering in the grout lines until I vacuum every nook and cranny. I also like that it will protect my baking soda from absorbing any stray odors that may affect the flavor of my cookies and baked goods.

I took a chance and ordered this one Used - Like New from Amazon warehouse deals. They said it had surface imperfections affecting less than 10% of the surface area. When mine arrived it had a sticker stuck on the lid and residue from another sticker on the side of the canister. It took around 10 drops of Goo Gone and doTerra wild orange to get all the residue off. I thought that was the only "surface imperfection" but then I noticed there are faint scratches along the circular rim of the lid, as if the lid was twisted against a slightly rough surface. Buffing with a drop of orange essential oil helped reduce the appearance of the scratches. Buying used saved me about $3 but be aware that if they say it is scratched, it really is scratched and may or may not have stickers all over it. Buy new if you don't keep Goo Gone on-hand...

In short, I am very, very pleased with this canister and am now wanting to purchase the 8 ounce size to store baking powder in. If you are considering stainless steel pantry storage containers, I highly recommend the thickness, heft and durability of this brand!

Vinyl Label: Oracal 631 color: Mint 055 • Font: KG Call Me Maybe • Craft Cutter: Silhouette

text_fidelity_a:
Allen 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack I placed this bike rack onto my 2003 Nissan Sentra. I knew this was the correct rack to buy thanks to the website that provides a list (Visit the fit list FIRST before purchasing an Allen bike rack): [...]

Anyway, since this bike rack had such good reviews and it was the right one for my car, I decided to buy it. Hooking it up was fairly easy. I'll admit, I struggled a little bit only because it was my fist attempt, but I know that it will be a peace of cake from now on. Once you get it right the first time, the future attempts will be perfectly easy. When I was finished, I put my body weight onto it to ensure it was sturdy enough for a bike, and it was definitely safe! That bike rack was not going to go anywhere! The straps and everything ensured it was sturdy and safe for the road!

I had to pick up my new bike today (A Schwinn Riverside 26" female bike that looks like this: [...]. As you can tell by the photo, my bike is a female bike. Because it is a female bike WITHOUT a straight bar, I had to purchase a second part that is also by Allen seen here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000ELSSZE/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i00. This bar is easy to install as well. It took me about ten seconds to place it onto my bike securely. This allowed me to easily put my bike onto the rack without any issues. Keep in mind, this is only for bikes that do NOT have a straight bar. You may or may not need this part. I needed it for mine.

Once I placed the bike onto the rack, I tightened up the straps. One thing I noticed is that the front wheel of the bike was not secure. It was free to turn as I drove, which would bang into my car, so I simply got a bungee cord and wrapped it in a way to prevent it from moving while I drove. I also got a bungee cord for the back wheel to prevent that wheel from spinning (this is not necessary, but I just prefer to do this). The peddles of the bike hit the bumper, so I would also recommend socks or clothes of some sort to be wrapped around them so they don't scratch the paint of your car.

Anyway, my bike and I made it home perfectly fine. The bike was very secure and sturdy on the bike rack. That bike was not going anywhere, even though I went up and down hills and made a lot of turns on my way home at around 50mph. I have not gone on the highway with it yet, but based on my experience so far, I am certain it is fine.

Overall, I recommend this product! It's great!
text_fidelity_b: Allen 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates Color: Watermelon. Skate Size: 7 (My normal shoe/boot size is 8-8.5 in US womens)
First, they are soooo cute! I love the color combo. I'm 50 yrs old and decided to get back into roller skating. I used to do this casually when I was in my teens, but was never exceptional at it. I thought this would be a fun way to get some more exercise in my life. So far its working! You engage so many muscles when roller skating. It takes balance, core and leg strength to keep from falling on your bum. These are made of vinyl so they are quite stiff at first and take some time break in. My hubby purchased these as a gift. He purchased according to the size chart and they fit well/snug with a thick sock. I normally wear a size 8 in U.S women’s shoes. When it comes to boots I typically buy 8.5 (to allow for thicker sock). Hubby purchased the size 7 skates as the chart indicated. This was just right. I thought they might be a bit tight at first. But with use, I realized the size was perfect. You want your foot to be held firmly as you will be moving around a lot. I imagine if they were looser, my foot would flex more and potentially cause strain in the foot muscles so I think the snug sizing is perfect. Measure your foot and look at size chart and you should be fine. I like that the skates have a metal base plate instead of plastic. This feels sturdier/safer. The wheels roll well on blacktop streets (even better on my hardwood floors inside my house). There are a couple things that were a bit odd. First the vinyl is so thick its a bit uncomfortable (specifically around the ankle) until they get worn in. And it takes a while to wear them in.
Second, the laces on one skate were a whole foot longer than the laces on the other skate. This trips out my OCD brain. I will have to replace them.

Overall, I think these are good skates for beginners (of all ages). They are made well and of good quality. Just be patient with the wear in period.
text_fidelity_b: Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates

text_fidelity_a:
Push-Up Pump [[VIDEOID:mo2U0MH5NGR4RTX]]This is a great little push up device. It's easy enough so that anyone can do a push-up or two with it, even your grandma. But, it also gives your upper body a really good workout even if you can do a lot of push-ups.

I really like how this device encourages great posture and discourages hyper-extension of joints. Push-ups would be a nearly perfect exercise if people didn't hyper extend their joints or over strain their weak parts when doing them. This device fixes everything by using your body weight to give you exercises that you can actually do.

This has helped me a ton with my upper body strength. It works, and I definitely recommend it.

Now, for the negatives.

The tension bands are a joke. Unless you either cut them apart or use all 65 lbs of them, they'll make a horrible snapping noise. You'll end up just throwing these away.

This won't last forever. It's not the sturdiest construction, and the design puts some weird strains on some of the joints, so it's only a matter of time before this falls apart. But you should get about a year of good use out of it, and by that time you'll be doing push-ups on your own.

The legs/feet of this should have been about twice as long, to make this sturdier. As it is, the only balanced position is with the seat placed on my upper stomach. If they were longer, then I could pick where I wanted to place my body on this.

And dismounting takes a lot of practice, and the fabric part peals off the first day you use it.

But overall, I'd heartily recommend it, especially if you've always dreamed of being able to do a lot of push-ups. No matter what your fitness level, this will definitely push you to the next level with push-ups.

Pros:
+Great way to work up to doing push-ups
+Great way to rapidly increase the number of push-ups you can do
+Fits away easily in a corner
+It's sturdy enough for what you need it for

Cons:
-You won't ever use the tension bands
-It's not the sturdiest construction. Expect it to break after about a year of use.
-Comes with fabric that's warping and pulling off
-The legs should have had more surface contact with the floor, to make this more steady
-I fell off this quite a few times when trying to stop doing push-ups, so it will take some time to get used to dismounting this device
text_fidelity_b: Push-Up Pump

Fishing Hook Giant 39960 28/0 Stainless Steel Shark Tuna Circle Big Game Saltwater Fantastic!!
I bought the hooks more for decoration, since nothing in our waters here have anything big enough to use a 28/0 hook for.
Tracking info said “...delivery 27 April to 7 May...”
They arrived on 23 April.

I don't understand the reviews:
"Made just like a real hook."
It IS a real hook. Just too big for non-anglers to realize it's real.

It will catch a fish, IF you fish in water that is home to something big enough. Like a 300+ pound grouper, or a big Great White off the coast of Australia. Of course, the rest of your gear would have to be able to handle it also. Rod, reel, line, leader. Everything you put out needs to be capable of handling it.

"Dulled hook to keep grandkids from poking themselves."
These hooks can be dangerous around small children. Teach them the fact that fishhooks of any size are not toys. They can hurt little people. Heck, if you're not careful, they can hurt big people.

But, these are REAL fishhooks. Excellent quality, strength and workmanship.
text_fidelity_b: Fishing Hook Giant 39960 28/0 Stainless Steel Shark Tuna Circle Big Game Saltwater

text_fidelity_a: Planet Bike Anatomic Relief System Classic Bike Seat- Men I ordered this bike because the saddle on my used Walmart (I admit it) road bike was killing my nether regions.  I have been riding for a year now and despite the origin of my bike, I have fallen in love with the sport and I usually go out for 15-20 mile rides and just enjoy the freedom it provides.  However, this season, my saddle became so painful that the fun was turning into sort of torture-endurance.  I decided to look for a new saddle but I hear so many stories of people spending all kinds of money trying to find the "right" saddle and if my bike is any indication, I don't have hundreds of dollars to spend to go through different saddles.  Anyway, I read the reviews on this saddle and being a bigger guy (240 lbs), I decided to give it a whirl based on the cheap cost.  Now, keep in mind that I also ordered a pair Pearl iZumi Men's Quest Cycling Shorts that I had read about on Amazon.  I say that because I figured a seat AND shorts might help.  On my first ride out with the saddle and the shorts, I was able to ride for 30 miles with hardly any pain!  I did notice that there would be a little pain when the bike short padding would get bunched up but after a readjustment, I was fine again.  It makes me wonder if the seat would have caused pain without the shorts.  I highly recommend buying shorts if you don't own any!  I wish I hadn't waited so long.  The padding makes a big difference.  I did notice the stickers coming off after the first ride but I don't really care about that.  I would rather have a plain seat then one with logos anyway.  I was surprised at how soft the seat was.  Some people have said that it is still a firm seat but after riding on my previous torture device, I feel that this is almost too padded.  I do feel that this is a great seat.  For the price, I figured I could give it a shot.  I'm definitely happy with the purchase!
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Anatomic Relief System Classic Bike Seat- Men

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Pop-Up Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 2/4 Person Tent Sets Up in 10 Seconds, Includes Pre-Assembled Poles, Adjustable Rainfly, and Taped Floor Seams I picked up the 2 person version of this tent with the hopes that if would be a good tent for my 11 year old to use for camping. I was pleasantly surprised by how roomy the tent is for a 2 person tent. Two people can comfortably lay sided by side in this tent with out issue. As others have suggested be careful taking it down, watch some youtube videos to see just how to do it as the instructions on the package are not the best for demonstrating it and if you don't do it right you could easily snap one of the poles.

Pros:
-This tent does go up in 10 seconds like the packaging suggests, though it may take you an additional minute to stake it in.
-Very roomy for a 2 person tent.
-Once you learn how to take it down it only takes about 20 seconds to go from being fully assembled to being in its bag.
-I used this tent in moderate rain and had no issues water in the tent.
-While the tent does not come with a foot print for it the bag the tent comes in has plenty of room to also hold a foot print.

Cons:
-You must take it down just right so you don't twist the poles the wrong way and snap them, be sure to practice this several times before going camping with it.
-You need to have some height to be able to take the tent down. In order to take down the tend you end up standing it on its side then have to pull it down from the top, as I said at the beginning of this review I bought this for my 11 year old son and he was not tall enough to take it down.
-Learning to take down the tent is a bit complicated but once you learn it then it is no problem.
-The size of the tent in the package is a bit large, it folds down into a circle that is larger than I would prefer; however, since it is rather flat finding a place to store or pack it is not usually a problem. Though certainly not a backpacking tent.
-Due to the tension in the poles that keeps the tent up it causes the zipper a bit difficult to zip up and I am worried that the zipper is going to break over time. There are two pull tabs for each zipper and the tension is greatest on the upper sides of the the zipper close to where the zipper starts (or finishes), I found that if I have the two pull tabs come together at the bottom (middle) of the zipper then I can avoid a lot of the tension.

Over all I really liked this tent, though my original use for it is not going to work. There is no way my 11 year old can take this tent down by himself and I am looking for other tents for him now. However, I am now using this as my personal tent when we go on scout camp outs and I love it.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Pop-Up Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 2/4 Person Tent Sets Up in 10 Seconds, Includes Pre-Assembled Poles, Adjustable Rainfly, and Taped Floor Seams

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ325 Alvita Ultimate Pedometer, Blue I do a lot of walking. A little over a year ago, I was diagnosed as being diabetic (type 2). I've been able to manage it by modifying my diet and daily exercise. I've been walking for at least 30 minutes every day, some days for an hour. Walking really brings down my blood sugar after eating. So I was happy to get one of these Omron pedometers to try out for a month.

Setting up the meter was pretty simple. You just had to install the battery and set the meter. Setting the meter entailed setting the time and putting in your stride length. To find your stride length you simply walk normally for ten steps - measure the distance (in inches), the divide by 10 (mine was 26 inches). There are some other settings - for example using km vs miles. Sounds more complicated than it is. Just be sure to read the instructions.

The meter comes with a few accessories such as a silicone case, a clip, and lanyard. The silicone case has a clip on the back of it, so that is what I used. I clipped the meter to the pocket-watch pocket on my blue-jeans. Which worked great, till I went out walking after lunch and came back without the meter. I'm guessing at some point the pedometer popped off and fell to the ground while I was walking. When I discovered it missing I retraced my steps and tried to find it - unsuccessfully. One of my co-workers even went out and tried to find it. Most of the path I walk in the after-noon is public sidewalks and tend to be heavily used by other walkers - so I'm guessing someone found it. I had the pedometer for about a week before losing it.

IMO -it was my own fault. I was wearing headphones at the time listening to an audiobook. And in hindsight, I should have attached the lanyard strap to the clip and hooked that to a belt-loop. I really suggest doing that.

The pedometer worked fine for me. I compared it to another meter and got similar readings. Operating the meter was easy - there are just three buttons. I really wish I hadn't lost mine.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ325 Alvita Ultimate Pedometer, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Lixada Pen Fishing Rod Collapsible Portable, Premium Mini Pocket Fishing Pole Ultralight Telescopic Fishing Rod 70.9in/82.7in (1.8M / 2.1M) I'm fairly impressed for a light duty compact travel fishing pole. The design is brilliant! Great for pan fish and as pictured, some big ones too if you know how to wear them out and not try to muscle a 10-20 pounder in if your lucky enough to hook one with this rig! You shouldn't be baiting and gearing up for big ones to start with using this pole. Like I said, pan fish as in blue gill, crappy, brook trout, small 2-4 lb bass etc is what this is designed for.

Think about finessing any big ones with your fly-fishing technique if you're lucky enough to hook a 5-10 or 20 pounder. Let them wear themselves out and then real them in once they're whooped and have no fight left. Make the fish work, not the rod... but you knew that right?

I have a small lite duty spin-casting reel with 8 lb line on it (typical lite gear) that I keep in a reel pouch with some "basic" tackle and a couple small lures. That and this pole inside my back-pack or saddle bag on the HD and I'm ready to fish anywhere I stop. All I need to rig up is either a small lure, or a hook and some bait. If there's fish in the water, dinner's pretty much a sure thing!

I'm blown away by the incompetence of some of these reviewers though. You just have to be smarter than the darn pole people!!!

First off, there are several 'presumably' carbon fiber sections that telescope in and out. Instead of forcing them as some are obviously doing, simply hold the section stationary below the one you want to move in or out. Then twist the section above the stationary one you're holding to loosen or tighten it as your pushing it in or pulling it out respectively.

Use the string guides to hold and "lightly" twist one way or the other. I can't stress enough to do this lightly folks! Don't get all Magilla Gorilla with it.

It doesn't take much effort to secure or loosen the sections. The very thin tip section should be held and twisted at the base where it is connected to the next section below it to prevent breaking it off (duh).

DON'T FORCE THEM! This isn't rocket science folks! It's simple grade school physics. Friction on a tapered shaft. A little lite twist and push or pull is all you need to extend or compact this pole. Mount your lite duty fishing reel on it, a bobber, hook and worm, and enjoy your day!!!
text_fidelity_b: Lixada Pen Fishing Rod Collapsible Portable, Premium Mini Pocket Fishing Pole Ultralight Telescopic Fishing Rod 70.9in/82.7in (1.8M / 2.1M)

text_fidelity_a: RCZZSUWE Professional Slingshots for Hunting, Catapult Shooting Slingshot Set for Adult, High Velocity Tactical Wrist Slingshot with Ammo Balls and Heavy Duty Launching Bands This is one heck of a little slingshot.  It is made well, very strong construction, easy to assemble, and it’s a nice looking product.  There is a little instruction insert, but it’s really just a matter of inserting the 2 bands into their slots and tightening the screws, then inserting the sites into their corresponding sites and using the included Allen wrench to tighten the slots.  I have another similar slingshot from Amazon that has sites, but that one does not have a level on the site whereas this one does.  I’m not sure I’ll need the level as I generally shoot straight, but it is a nice extra feature that I am going to see if I can try shooting with it horizontal.  As with my other slingshot, I have the same issue with slingshot and that is that the handle really needs to be longer. It is only 3 inches from the end of the handle to where the handle meets or intersects with the body.  I guess I don’t understand why these otherwise great slingshots have such  short handles.  The end of the handle digs into the palm of my hand when I hold it so can cause blisters.  I will also be getting some better straps but the two that were included should be okay for a bit.  Overall this is really a very cool slingshot that I feel is reasonably priced and it even came with some ammo.

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series I live in an apartment in Arizona, and I wanted a quality inflatable boat I could take to the local lakes. After researching my options, IM4 appeared to be the top boat.

Although manufacturer claims it is a 4 person boat, it is NOT true. Two people can be comfortable in this boat, three is pushing it. With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

Update from 10/05/2012. On my recent trip to the lake I broke one of the ores. The plastic on the coupling broke when I did five spirited rows, I was upset. I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series

We took the children around as a group and this light lit the way for all the adults (no one had brought a flashlight) and made it easy for our son to spot his parents in the crowd, ensuring he didn't get to far ahead of the group.

I set the Luci to charge in a windowsill for about 8 hours of sunlight, deflated it and stored it flat on a shelf until it was needed Halloween night, about two weeks later. It lit up and glowed for several hours that night without even flickering or dimming. Multiple people admired it, switching it on and off through it's various settings of low, high, flash and off. It even got curious inquiries and compliments from strangers out with their children as well.

Not only is this a great light to have on hand for emergencies but it's going to prove useful during family camp outs (we camp as a family about 6 times per year and my husband and son rack up another 3-6 camp outs with boy scouts). I also plan on using it during night time activities at New Year's and July 4th. I love that I don't have to suddenly worry about batteries as the sun is sinking in the sky during busy, eventful holidays when it would be difficult to run to the store in all the traffic - if you can even get to the store because the roads have been shut down for the parade/fireworks show/trick or treaters. text_fidelity_a:
Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote This is a comfortable back pack.
The selling point for me was that it was listed to be able to accept an additional water bladder. And for me, (I hike in the Phoenix, AZ area mountains during the midday summer heat) that is important. Two 3liter bladders are a standard for me. Normally, I have to move up to my 35 litter backpack during the summer because the straps on my other packs are too narrow to adequately support the weight of two 3liter bladders (6 kilos or about 13lbs) in addition to my emergency first aid supplies, food, phone, and anything else I have. In total, about 25lbs (a little more than 11 kilos).

So it was a pleasant surprise that the straps on this 20 liter pack were almost as wide as the straps on my 35 liter pack. Making this pack easily able to comfortably carry the weight.

Also the waist belt has molle webbing for attaching additional things. For me, that's a phone carrier on one side and a 4x6 pouch on the other for some trail snacks (if I need the nourishment on the trail). A big plus. I don't have to remove the backpack to have a snack or to put the empty wrapper back in the pouch.
The waist belt also helps keep everything stable when I am trail running (probably about half of my normal 10 mile hike is trail running)

The padding on this backpack is much better than any of my other backpacks regardless of size. (I have 3l,6l,12l,18l,20l,25l,30l, and 35l backpacks.) Yes, I have a lot because I've never been able to find a nearly perfect fit for my needs, until now.

The bladder - this is a high quality bladder. (I now have four of them.) It has a nice high water flow. I'm easily drinking more during my hike because of this high flow rate. With my other bladders, I averaged about 1 liter an hour consumption. With these bladders, I average 1.5 liters an hour consumption. I have my garmin watch set to give a reminder every 8 minutes to drink water. So with the old bladders and the new Source bladders, I was drinking at the same intervals, it's just easier to drink through the Source drinking tube than the other ones resulting in the higher consumption.

Strap management - this thing has elastic on each of the straps to hold the excess strapping. Wow, so nice. No Irish pennants (marine corps terminology referring to the the stray threads sticking out on clothing) flying all over the place

text_fidelity_a:
UVPaqlite Tooblite I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased, this was reasonably impressive. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 60 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. Even by 90 minutes, it's still faintly visible, but only just barely.

Out of the 4 UVPaqlite items I purchased, this didn't glow as strong or last as long as the UVPaqlite packets - however, that seemed natural, given its tubular design (less surface area exposed to the viewer). The clear resin had a lot of bubbles, which seemed to diffuse the glow a bit - making for a more even light, but also limiting its range. However, the tubular design is also its biggest strength. Compared to the UVPaqlite packets - which are fairly rugged in their own right - this seems much more durable, as well as convenient to carry or mount. As such, I mounted this next to my quick-release home shotgun mount. In the event the lights immediately go out, I can quickly - even before my eyes have adjusted - find my flashlight and unlock the shotgun, should I need it.

If you need stronger and longer lasting light, I recommend the UVPaqlite vacuum-sealed packets. Both the [[ASIN:B00698NBYE UVPaqlite Medium]] and [[ASIN:B00698HB1I UVPaqlite Mini]] out-performed the Tooblites I bought, as far as effective brightness. However, consider that the Tooblite shape is more convenient for certain tasks. As well, while these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products have their purposes, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescence glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.
text_fidelity_b: UVPaqlite Tooblite

We live in a hot weather, water-centric state and have a large number of beach towels, so we have a pretty strong, large range of items by which we can compare this beach towel. In the end, we are not overly impressed with this Northwest NCAA Michigan Wolverines Unisex-Adult Beach Towel.

It does look decent - the design is nice - the blue does look like a nice blue and the yellow a nice yellow - on track with the school’s colors. That said, it IS splotchy - the coloring has some splotchy looks to the blue portions which I try to show in the photos.. When you get up to it - even from a distance - it is like not all the threads were colored. Also, why does it say it’s “Psychedelic?” When I was growing up that word was used to describe things that were part of that 60s-70s counter culture, designed, flared kind of look, not two solid colors as part of a well known logo. We both feel like the towel itself is very thin, and being this thin would likely not do great for drying one off. It would be something we would keep as a backup or the towel we’d throw on the chair, but not use for actually drying. We are not 100% sure we’re even going to give it to her and in the end we are lukewarm on it.
text_fidelity_b: Northwest NCAA Unisex-Adult Beach Towel

Now, I'm an engineer and trust me, I know what I'm doing. I tried different settings for sensor sensitivity (only high, mid and low are available). At high setting it keeps taking pictures every second, regardless of any motion in front of the camera. At mid setting, it only takes a picture of I walk in right front of it. Anything past 5-6 ft isn't detected at all. Low setting only works if I put my face right in front of the camera (1-2 ft). Keep in mind that I bought 2 of these cameras (yes I know, should have tried one first). Both work identically and both are totally useless for detecting game or people past 6 feet.
So, I just wasted money on no-name junk products made of Chinesium. Lesson learned.....again. I'm not rich enough to buy cheap things. Buy good, well knows brands! Buy once, cry once!.

text_fidelity_a:
Razor A5 Lux Scooter You will be singing praises to the designer if this wheel if you ever have to repair a flat or ever just add air. I have 4 different pumps and none will fit the design of the wheel and tube stem.

To repair or replace the tube - good luck! You need to remove one bolt through the hub, holding the same allen bit on both sides at the same time (hope you have 2!). There are two little hub components that fall out when the wheel comes out. Don't lose them! Then there are four bolt on one side of the wheel and four nuts on the other side. Don't drop any! When you get the wheel apart there is ANOTHER loose hub part that falls out. How many pieces are we dealing with now? Not counting the two bit sets I have out. Yikes!

Hopefully you have a spare or patch kit. After you fix or replace the tube, you have to line the wheel halves up with each other, and the tube stem. Don't forget to put the inner hub lose piece in. And don't worry about lining it up because there is no way to. You'll end up just rattling the wheel around until the bolt finds it's way in. But first you have to hold all those nuts in while you screw the four bolts back in. THEN hold the wheel to the scooter AND the two outer hub components while you put the FINAL bolt back in - also holding both ends so the bolt will screw in. Remember, you have to shake the scooter and all those components until the bolt finds it's way to that inner hub piece. It's helpful if you have two other people to help.

So now that you have it all back together get your needle nose pliers to pull the stem out so you can attach a pump. Pump up to 60 PSI and cross your fingers. Oh, the patch didn't take? Don't worry, just repeat all those previous steps!

Try not to think how you just paid $130 bucks for a scooter, or how the designer is on the beach in the Caribbean.

One star left only because my kid likes it. LOL
text_fidelity_b: Razor A5 Lux Scooter

text_fidelity_a:
QOGIR Resistance Trainer for Disc Golf, Practice Backhand or Forehand Throws to Improve Your Disc Golf Technique, Increase Strength in Your Pull Through, Gain Extra Distance, Disc Shaped Grip. A little background: I'm a righty, but due to disc-elbow problems (tennis elbow for disc golfers) I'm training my left arm to throw. The control issues are coming around, however so far I'm only getting about half the distance. When I started with the right arm years ago I noticed growth in the muscle over time as my distance improved. Hence my interest in this training device for the left arm. I want to quickly get back to the same success with the left arm.

I hooked this up to a couple of wall studs in my partially finished basement. After using it several times I can tell it's giving the arm a workout. I tried all three band combinations and can definitely tell the difference.

One concern is that the tension on the disc requires a very firm grip. Fortunately the device comes with a safety strap to keep the disc attached to your arm should your grip slip. My concern is that it might teach me to grip more firmly than needed on the course. I think I can adjust for that, so it may be a non-concern.

If you don't have something firm to attach to like a tree or a wall stud, the kit includes a piece to put into a door frame. A word of caution is to only use this from the side of the door where you would be pulling the door shut. You definitely don't want the door to open while you have the disc pulled back in full tension and have that door piece come flying at you.

My only complaint is that I found no instructions. It is possible that I overlooked them in the box and tossed them out. I was able to find what I needed in the Amazon description.

I'm betting that the next few weeks will see an improvement in my lefty distance!
text_fidelity_b: QOGIR Resistance Trainer for Disc Golf, Practice Backhand or Forehand Throws to Improve Your Disc Golf Technique, Increase Strength in Your Pull Through, Gain Extra Distance, Disc Shaped Grip.
